correctness_review.method: manual read of label/section/id/itype vs. assigned_category for a 60-field random sample of the resolved held-out fields, drawn from heldout_sample_for_manual_review.json

unresolved_characterization.method: manual read of all 387 unresolved held-out fields
unresolved_characterization.finding: Overwhelmingly one-off, hyper-specific skill-gate yes/no questions unique to a single job posting (e.g. Apptronik's 'Do you have at least N years of experience with <specific tech stack>?', worded differently per posting) plus a handful of one-off portfolio/GitHub-link phrasings and 2 Korean file-upload labels. These are genuine long-tail phrasing variance, not a systematic taxonomy gap -- each would need to be seen verbatim to cluster, since the wording is unique per job req rather than a recurring question type. Not evidence the taxonomy needs new categories; it's the expected residual of a natural-language label-matching approach.
